label: Late copy-phase steps; saturates at step 5 of length-3 sequences
explanation: Only fires in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original tokens or on <DEL>, and mostly on the last two outputs (to_go <= 1 holds 95% of activation mass). Its core is the final step (t=5) of length-3 sequences: active on 99.7% of those steps, with the largest activations (top examples like a m z <DEL> a [m]), and that one case alone carries 56% of the mass. In longer sequences it is sparse (about 1-5% of late copy steps) and weak, more likely when the input token is m or i (also o, b). Within the to_go <= 1 region I found nothing else that predicts which steps fire, so precision is low (dev F1 0.42, mass recall 0.75).
